rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Placed in service in 2025" = true → helper "Limit for a 2025 vehicle"] [helper "Placed in service in 2025" = false → helper "Limit for the vehicle's 2025 year of recovery"]
rulings.model: The 2025 amounts ($20,200 with the special allowance, $12,200 without) and the earlier-year amounts match the tables. But line 7 always applies the passenger-automobile limit, even when the filer says the vehicle is not a passenger automobile. The text says the limits apply "For any passenger automobile", and those vehicles have no refusal.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; restatement accepted. Line 7 is a line of the Pub. 946 worksheet for passenger automobiles and is shown for every vehicle, but it limits only a passenger automobile: for a vehicle that is not one, the special allowance, the section 179 deduction and MACRS take the scveh.passenger = false branches, which do not read it (checked: a $60,000 truck placed in service in 2025 with the 100% allowance gets $60,000, a passenger automobile $20,200).

A vehicle that is not a passenger automobile is not limited.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Standard mileage rate or actual expenses" = 'standard' → helper "Standard mileage amount plus parking fees and tolls"] [helper "Standard mileage rate or actual expenses" = 'actual' → helper "Business portion of the operating expenses plus parking fees and tolls"]
rulings.model: The standard branch (miles x 0.70 plus parking and tolls) and the business portion of operating expenses agree with the text, but no refusal is shown for this rule: 'You can't use actual expenses for a leased vehicle if you previously used the standard mileage rate for that vehicle.' The screen that asks about earlier standard mileage use only refuses at column (d), which the leased path does not use.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding (BUG-0310, open, T-173); i1040sc p. 6: "You can't use actual expenses for a leased vehicle if you previously used the standard mileage rate for that vehicle." The screen's refusal is on scveh.cost, which a leased vehicle does not read; stage14.veh.leased_actual with the screen answered Yes still completes. The rest of the restatement matches.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Standard mileage rate or actual expenses" = 'standard' → helper "Standard mileage amount plus parking fees and tolls"] [helper "Standard mileage rate or actual expenses" = 'actual' → helper "Business portion of the operating expenses plus parking fees and tolls"]
rulings.model: The standard branch (miles × $0.70 plus parking and tolls) and the actual branch match the instructions, but nothing blocks the actual branch for a leased vehicle with earlier standard mileage use. The IRS text says 'You can't use actual expenses for a leased vehicle if you previously used the standard mileage rate for that vehicle.'
rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal located elsewhere; restatement accepted. A vehicle for which the standard mileage rate was used in an earlier year, leased or owned, is refused through scveh.screen ('you used the standard mileage rate for it in an earlier year'), so a leased vehicle that reaches actual expenses has never used the standard rate.

rulings.model: The standard branch matches ("Multiply the number of business miles driven by 0.70... Add to this amount your parking fees and tolls"). For actual expenses, the text says only "Include on line 9 the business portion of expenses for gasoline, oil, repairs, insurance, license plates, etc." It does not say whether parking fees and tolls are added in full under that method.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; restatement accepted. The parking input asks only for parking fees and tolls for the vehicle's business use, and Pub. 463 lists tolls and parking fees among actual car expenses (p. 21); being for business use only, they are added in full, as on the standard mileage rate branch.
